title: Remote plugin-manifest backends are rebuilt without settings deps and keyed by full entry fingerprint
answers: How does the router detect a remote plugin deployment moved to a new host and reload it?
Why do remote/plugins_url-discovered plugins not expose settings, health, resources, proxy?
Backend for a plugin-manifests target doesn't refresh when its deployment host changes
body:
Root cause/mechanism: pkg/router/plugin_manifests.go:pluginManifestsTarget.poll builds each remote backend via router.NewPluginBackend, but explicitly nils deps.PluginClient, ContextProvider, PluginSettings, and DualWrite before calling it, because remote deployments (discovered from plugins_url) have no local settings/gRPC client access yet.
Invariant: backend identity/reload is driven by pluginDeploymentKey (sha256 of the whole marshaled definition.PluginDeployment, including Host) — any field in that struct changing (e.g. deployment host) must change the key so the dirty channel fires and the router swaps in a fresh pluginDeploymentBackend; see pkg/router/plugin_manifests_test.go:TestPluginManifestsTargetReloadsOnHostChange.
Constraints: real gRPC client wiring for these remote backends (the TODO in poll's client-provider func) is deferred to a follow-up PR — don't assume ServeHTTP on these backends does real proxying yet.
applies: pkg/router plugin-manifests discovery/reload path for remote (plugins_url) plugin deployments
says: Why don't remotely discovered plugins show settings or health status?
Remote plugin deployment moved to new host but didn't reload.
How does the system detect a remote plugin host change?
Plugins from URL lack settings, health, and resource endpoints.
Remote plugin requires manual restart after changing deployment location.
